text:
jordan-cs: Customer escalation: multiple 400s for /v1/invoke hitting the price_lookup tool after yesterday's schema change. Error: \"schema validation failed: 'amount' expected number, got string\". Request ID: abc123. @maria-support can you triage?

maria-support: on it — can you paste the exact payload and any headers (auth token masked) + a sample request_id?

jordan-cs: here you go (removed customer keys):
```json
{
  \"tool\": \"price_lookup\",
  \"args\": {
    \"item_id\": \"sku_999\",
    \"amount\": \"100\",    // customer sends string
    \"currency\": \"USD\"
  }
}
```
Response: 400 + body: \"schema error: args.amount: expected number, got string\"

ben-platform: I can repro locally with the same payload hitting the invoke runtime. Validator is strict now after PR #4321 (schema tightening) — it rejects string amounts.

olivia-eng: that PR was meant to prevent silent rounding bugs but we missed compatibility shims. Was there a feature flag?

ben-platform: no feature flag, the schema change landed in runtime schema v2.0 and rollout was gradual but looks like some customer traffic hit the stricter validators in prod.

alice-ml: FYI our toolcall golden-eval CI started failing around the same commit. The golden prompt suite has a case that passes string amounts and expects the service to coerce. CI shows 7 failures referencing price_lookup args schema.

ci-bot: CI results: https://ci.internal/runs/5402 — failing tests: price_lookup/golden/amount_string_coercion, price_lookup/invoke_smoke_001, toolcall-regression-suite/price_args_type

maria-support: customer wants a workaround ASAP. Can we add a permissive coercion in the validator for numbers represented as strings? That would be the fastest fix.

ben-platform: quick mitigation: add a small compatibility layer in the runtime that tries to coerce numeric strings to numbers for known fields (amount, quantity, price). Example patch:
```js
// before validation
if (typeof args.amount === 'string' && /^\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?$/.test(args.amount)) {
  args.amount = Number(args.amount)
}
```
This avoids schema change and keeps strictness for other types.

olivia-eng: agreed. Let's ship a hotfix to canary tomorrow morning, then to prod if canary is green. Also add a rollback for the schema enforcement in that PR.

alice-ml: I'll update the golden prompt suite to include a negative test (ensure we reject non-numeric garbage like \"one hundred\") and a positive test for numeric strings so we don't regress. We should also add the coercion case to unit tests.

jordan-cs: customer acceptance criteria: 1) their requests succeed again, 2) we avoid silent mis-parses. They can accept coercion as a temporary workaround.

maria-support: I'll notify the customer and offer a short-term workaround: cast amount to number client-side, and we'll follow up when hotfix is deployed.

ben-platform: creating ticket INF-2387 for runtime coercion hotfix + test updates + rollback plan. Assigning to olivia-eng for release.

olivia-eng: taking INF-2387. Plan: patch validator coercion + unit tests today, canary deploy in eu-west-1 tomorrow 08:00 UTC, monitor logs for 30m, then gradual roll to remaining regions.

ci-bot: Also scheduled: update golden eval job to run against the canary image so CI catches these earlier — reopening flaky test policy.

maria-support: thanks all :thumbsup: I'll keep the customer updated and close the loop after canary.

jordan-cs: appreciated. follow-up: create a short postmortem note after release summarizing timeline and decision to tighten schema in the future with a feature flag.
